annotations.keyFindings: A prescribing prompt was followed by a fall in the HPCIA share from 24 to 13 percent over 20 weeks in three clinics, with amoxicillin-clavulanate up 4 points and no change in 7-day re-consultation.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after comparison in three clinics; no adjustment for season; reasons entered were brief.

annotations.keyFindings: Monthly benchmarking letters were followed by a relative 18 percent fall in the HPCIA share against 3 percent in comparison practices, larger where a named stewardship lead existed.
annotations.limitations: Self-selected practices with higher baseline use; regression to the mean possible; no clinical outcomes.

annotations.keyFindings: Guidelines combined with audit and feedback were followed by lower HPCIA use in nine of ten studies that measured it; guidelines alone showed little change.
annotations.limitations: Twelve of fourteen studies were before-after designs at serious risk of bias; indicators too heterogeneous to pool; search ended in 2022.

annotations.keyFindings: Cultures were submitted for 11 percent of cats and 19 percent of dogs with lower urinary tract signs; 27 percent of cultured cats and 62 percent of cultured dogs grew bacteria.
annotations.limitations: Clinics self-selected; reasons for not culturing recorded inconsistently.

annotations.keyFindings: Owner satisfaction did not depend on receiving an antimicrobial when the diagnosis was explained and a recheck plan given; cat owners more often expected difficulty giving tablets.
annotations.limitations: Single region, 46 percent response, self-reported expectations after the visit.

annotations.keyFindings: Weekly drug-class indicators extracted from practice management systems matched case-note review for 94 percent of prescriptions; indication-specific indicators were unreliable because only 61 percent had a coded reason.
annotations.limitations: Six clinics using two software systems; one reviewer per note.

annotations.keyFindings: Veterinary surgeons chose long-acting injections for cats because tablets are hard to give, courses may not be completed, consultations are short and owners might leave; they wanted tablet-giving support from nurses.
annotations.limitations: Volunteer participants; one country; no owner perspective.

claims.text: In three small-animal clinics, the share of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions that were HPCIAs fell from 24 to 13 percent over 20 weeks after a prescribing prompt was introduced.
claims.passage: the share of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions that were HPCIAs fell from 24 to 13 percent
claims.interpretation: Supports the prompt as the first change idea; uncontrolled, so the size of change is a planning value only.

claims.text: Practices receiving monthly benchmarking feedback reduced their HPCIA share by a relative 18 percent over six months, against 3 percent in comparison practices.
claims.passage: Over six months the HPCIA share fell by a relative 18 percent in practices receiving feedback and by 3 percent in comparison practices.
claims.interpretation: Supports monthly clinic feedback as part of the change package.

claims.text: Drug-class indicators extracted weekly from practice management systems matched case-note review for 94 percent of prescriptions.
claims.passage: Automated extraction correctly identified the drug class, including highest-priority critically important antimicrobials, for 94 percent of prescriptions.
claims.interpretation: The weekly HPCIA share can be measured without reading notes; indication-specific measures need manual sampling.

claims.text: Among cats with lower urinary tract signs that were cultured, only 27 percent grew bacteria.
claims.passage: Of cats with lower urinary tract signs that had a urine culture, 27 percent grew bacteria, compared with 62 percent of cultured dogs.
claims.interpretation: Free culture in cats is likely to show that many treated cats had no bacterial infection.

claims.text: Veterinary surgeons chose long-acting injections for cats because of tablet difficulty, doubts about course completion, short consultations and fear of losing clients.
claims.passage: Participants described difficulty giving tablets to cats, doubts about whether owners would complete a course, short consultation times and a fear that owners would move to another practice if sent home with tablets.
claims.interpretation: Tablet-giving support for owners belongs in the change package.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A prescribing prompt (24 to 13 percent) and monthly benchmarking feedback (relative fall of 18 against 3 percent) were each followed by lower HPCIA use, and a review of fourteen mostly uncontrolled studies found guidelines work mainly when combined with feedback. Weekly drug-class indicators can be extracted reliably from practice software, while indication-specific indicators cannot. Most cultured cats with urinary signs grew nothing. Prescribers choose injections for cats largely because tablets are hard to give, and owners stay satisfied when the reason for not prescribing is explained. No record measured clinical outcomes beyond re-consultation, and substitution towards amoxicillin-clavulanate was seen after a prompt.
gradeRationale: Consistent direction across a before-after report, a controlled before-after comparison and a review of mostly uncontrolled studies, but serious risk of bias from secular trends and self-selection and no clinical outcome data. Certainty that the change package lowers HPCIA use is low; certainty about effects on animal outcomes is very low.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims recorded with passages; overall certainty low.
